summary: Deep adversarial probe of komihash, a5hash and MuseAir under a uniformly random seed: structure/key-free search, weak-seed classes, full differential scan, hill-climb, multi-seed SMT; independent reproduction; per-hash bits score

per_hash.best_verified_pair: len 64 B (L = 8 words; identical rate at 65..127 B with any common suffix). m = c1675e0bb980a575 84142e08970abc66 63f1ee08469ccdac 9ff735ab278a84ba 000000000000805e 6c0ce934cf66d4e0 737a74e5f8908faf afcc5252147fbc5b (LE words w0..w7), m' = m with bit 0 of byte 0 and of byte 8 flipped (c1->c0, 84->85). Structure: w1 = w0 ^ IVAL2 ^ 1, w5 = w4 ^ IVAL6, w4 = 0x5e8<<52 (tuned against the skew of the preseeded S5). Example colliding seed: 0 (also 0x0123456789abcdef); non-colliding seeds exist (e.g. 0x61954dcc47b1e89d). Equivalent independent construction (komihash-structure): efcdab8967452301 aabedb8a49cf3a12 2222000000000000 3333000000000000 000000000000a05e 6c0ce934cf66f4e0 6666000000000000 7777000000000000 vs bit 0 of bytes 0 and 8 flipped, y = 0x5ea<<52, rate 0.91056 at 2^28.
per_hash.kind: deterministic-trail (high-probability differential, NOT key-free): eps = 0.9106 for a fixed pair differing in 2 bits. Mechanism (proved from source, predicate == collision on 2^29 seeds): for 64..127 B exactly one HASHLOOP64 iteration runs; lane seeds Seed2..4 = IVAL2..4 ^ S1 and Seed6..8 = IVAL6..8 ^ S5 are PUBLIC XOR offsets of the two state words and the exit combine XORs the lane products symmetrically except that each hi half is added to a different word S5 ^ IVAL_k. With w1 = w0^IVAL2^1, w5 = w4^IVAL6 lanes 0,1 compute u*v and (u^1)*v; flipping bit 0 of w0,w1 swaps them; collision iff (S5+h0)^(S6+h1) == (S5+h1)^(S6+h0), S6 = S5^IVAL6. h1-h0 in {0,+-1}: certain when lo(uv)+-v does not carry (Pr = 1 - E[v]/2^64, v = w4^S5), else exactly 3/4 (IVAL6 ends in binary ...1100). Preseeded S5 = B + hi(A*B) is skewed (bit 63 set w.p. 0.281, A/B carry only the even/odd seed bits), so w4 = 0x5e8<<52 gives E[v]/2^64 = 0.357 and eps = 1 - 0.357/4 = 0.9107. Bit on the second operand instead: exactly 7/8 (939508211/2^30); lanes (2,3): 3/4; other lane pairs: 1/2.
per_hash.null_resolution: Effect confined to 64..127 B: 0/2^28 at 63, 128 (either block) and 192 B (verified). No public-only (key-free) path exists: every message word is XORed with S1 or S5 before any multiply in every length class; tails injective with length markers (proved by inspection, komihash-structure). Seed-expanded S5' never equals 0, 1, 2^63, 2^64-1 or IVAL6 (exact enumeration over all 2^64 seeds, komihash-weakseed; unverified but exact); densest S5' value has 268 preimages (2^-55.9, lower bound; unverified, immaterial). Null scans: prior complement family (all-ones on both fold operands, single/double word complements at every 16-byte position, length-boundary and zero-padding pairs) 0 in 2^32 seeds; komihash-foldscan 4910 cells (lengths 1..40,48,63,64,65,96,128,160,200; word XOR bit 0/31/32/63, ADD +-1/+-2^32/+2^63 at 8-aligned offsets and L-8, byte+1 at every byte, HASH16-operand and lane pairs ADD-both/opposite/XOR-both with 1, 2^32, 2^63) x 2^24 seeds and 115 cells x 2^30: 0 collisions, max per-bit |z| 3.56 (representative cell re-verified 0/(2^31+2^28)); komihash-structure 7008 single-byte/word differences at every position of lengths 1..63 x 2^23: 0; komihash-hillclimb (1+1)-ES 12 islands x 720 s, top-5 pairs null at 2^28 (max |z| 3.55); z3 multi-seed queries (K=2, len 15/31): unknown at 100-600 s (no information). Not searched: >=128-byte structures beyond this pair, other lane permutations / joint low-bit tuning (0.9106 is the best found, conjectured near-optimal for lanes (0,1)), the streaming API.

per_hash.hash: a5hash v5.21, 64-bit output (SMHasher3 hashes/a5hash.cpp; upstream v5.25 has the same init structure, not vector-checked)
per_hash.best_verified_pair: len 6615 B (L = 826.9 words). m = e0aa5c8e00000000 8877665544332211 || F, m' = e0aa5c8e00000000 1122334455667788 || F, F = any common 6599 bytes (run used byte i = (7i+3) mod 256; verifier also used zeros and splitmix bytes). First block word W0 = lu32(m)<<32 | lu32(m+4) = 0x8e5caae000000000 = W*; collision iff Seed1_init == W* (first block operand W0 ^ Seed1_init = 0, product 0, state (val01,val10) independent of bytes 8..15). Example colliding seed 0xbdd730a20c451ba4 (h = 9cda28706bf2e550 for both); class = 118 * 2^19 seeds exactly.
per_hash.kind: weak-seed-trail (dead multiplier on a heavy value of the seed-expanded state). Seed1_init = lo64(X*Y), X = K2^len^(seed&0xAA..), Y = K1^len^(seed&0x55..): the even bit positions of X and the odd ones of Y are fixed by the length, so v2(Seed1_init) = v2(X)+v2(Y) is controlled by len; at len 6615, (v2(X),v2(Y)) = (20,17) costs 19 seed bits and the residual 27-bit product is hit by 118 of the 2^26 remaining relevant assignments; upper seed bits free. Density 118*2^-45 = 2^-38.117 exactly (complete enumeration by claimant and verifier: 472 low-47-bit patterns x 2^17). Other exact points: len 15 (13136 seeds, 2^-50.32, 51.2 bits), len 16 (5626 seeds, 2^-51.54, 52.5 bits), len 137687 (54*2^-43, 51.3 bits), len 15866327 (2^-32 exactly, 52.9 bits). Also proved: Seed2_init bit 63 = 0 for every seed; Seed1_init even for every odd length.
per_hash.null_resolution: No public-only path in the 64-bit hash (every message word XORed into Seed1/Seed2, both halves of the seeded product, before any multiply; proved by inspection). Structured pairs on the fully seeded path: 143 pairs (complements, 2^63 on one/both operands, val01/val10 offsets, tail/block swaps, +-1, tail-only, cross-length zero messages, block2 := block1^(55..,AA..)) x 2^26: 0 collisions, max |z| 4.01 (a5hash-structure); a5hash-foldscan 4873 cells x 2^24 (random base) + x 2^22 (zero base) + x 2^22 (0xFF base) + 39 cells x 2^30: 0 collisions, max per-bit |z| 4.19 (threshold 5.59); a5hash-hillclimb ~2^22.7 candidate pairs (~2^38 seed evaluations), top-50 null at 2^28 (max |z| 3.94); a5hash-smt: 19/20 z3 multi-seed queries unknown at 420 s, len 1 K=2 UNSAT (no information); output bits of single messages unbiased (|z| <= 3.85 at 2^26). Not done: exhaustive search over lengths for the minimum of log2(L/eps) (the 6615 came from a heuristic length search; 4567 (33-bit residual) and the 57-bit residual at len <= 16 not enumerated), heavy values of Seed2_init = hi(XY), a5hash_32.
per_hash.provenance: Found by a5hash-structure (enum_mode.c, search_len.py); the same mechanism found independently at smaller rates by a5hash-weakseed (exact fibres, beam search), a5hash-foldscan (greedy prefix enumeration, 2^-53.5 at 17 B) and a5hash-smt (S2i heavy values, 2^-56.7). Verified: verify-a5hash-structure (own derive.c enumeration 118*2^19 seeds; stratified sampling 1821 hits in 2^30 stratum seeds vs 1888+-44 expected -> 2^-38.17; 457/2^28 with an unrelated fill; controls 0/2^30 + 0/2^28; class-sampled 65535/65535 x 3 fills; example seed collides; second verifier: len-6615 v2=35 variant exact 136*2^17 seeds, all 17825792 collide), verify-a5hash-weakseed (len 15 fibre exactly 13136 by complete lifting; len 16 fibre 5626 two independent ways; 0/2^28-2^30 random), verify-a5hash-smt (len 16 S2i class exactly 159 seeds; len 24 class exactly 104 seeds, 0/2^34 random). Synthesis re-run: ./measure class 16 3 7 -> 65535/65535, example seed collides, neighbour differs. All implementations reproduce SMHasher3 _ComputedVerifyImpl 0xADDE79B3. per_hash.best_verified_pair: len 17 B (L = 17/8 words). m = 00ddc7f65b30ce60d6 0000000000000000, m' = 00ddc7f65b30ce60d6 00000000000000ff (differ in byte 16 only). c = lu32(m+1)<<32 | lu32(m+5) = 0x5bf6c7ddd660ce30 = -Seed3 mod 2^64, so (c+Seed3)(d+Seed4) = 0 for every d and byte 16 (read only into d) is dead. Also verified: len 24 f3d33b4c87024567ddc7f65b30ce60d6fa7b966b1c4d42b3 / ...fb7b966b1c4d42b3 (2^30) and len 32 f3d33b4c87024567a47efcde0e5daaa0ddc7f65b30ce60d6924b4c57129b4ad6 / ...7d86e7de75de69d7 (2^30+2^28+2^20); equal-product pairs (X,Y)->(2X,Y/2) also collide.
per_hash.kind: key-free (eps = 1 for every seed, both output words). Seed3 = 0xA4093822299F31D0, Seed4 = 0xC0AC29B7C97C50DD and Seed5..8 are unseeded constants, so the products (c+K3)(d+K4) [17..32 B, last two words], (lu64(16)+K3)(lu64(24)+K4) [33..64 B] and lanes (m1+K3)(m5+K4), (m2+K5)(m6+K6), (m3+K7)(m7+K8) of the first 64-byte block [>64 B] are public functions of the message; any u*v = u'*v' collides for every seed, and u = 0 makes the partner word dead (2^64-way multicollisions) at every length >= 17. The 64-bit a5hash is NOT affected (0 collisions on all these pairs). Score: log2(17/8) = 1.1 bits (1.6 if L is rounded up to whole words), MUM tier.
per_hash.null_resolution: Lengths <= 16 (short path: (a + Seed1) with seeded Seed1) have no key-free pair; the weak-seed class analogue a = -w64 was derived but not run. 128-bit outputs on the foldscan's 4873 generic cells: 0 collisions at 2^24/2^30 (max per-bit |z| 5.10 < 5.59 threshold); a5hash-hillclimb 128-bit classes null at 2^28.

per_hash.best_verified_pair: len 17 B (L = 17/8 words), all four variants. m = 95035294f2065da4d5aebfbee6b7dcf275, m' = f966f58b6a8749a4726e03c846fee90b1d (construction A: distinct tails t,t' with the 16-byte prefix compensated through the public bijection read_short: read(p') = read(p) ^ G(t) ^ G(t')). Also verified key-free at len 32 (equal prefixes): 00..00 a8060a6505df5a48b250257b2d99c3c1 / a8060aa505df5a48b350257b2d99c3c1 (komihash-smt; x' = x+2^62, y' = y+1); 1011..1e1f 3edfaa2763ccd3e8f8e5d00dc73236e4 / 99b0519651a489b815f5132911d93af1 (foldscan, lattice); 2d875180e4a6eb70eeafa3bb393d507e 1e66dca9113ab21ceed7f56d0d9d3350 / b7e1cbe5113ab21c84d4f56d94faeb6c (hillclimb, carry DP); 0001..0e0f 94332321545d545229e6bec106900910 / f7a5cb9102350a6246f9f9dd503ffe1c (museair-smt, lattice). bfast-only extras (verified): len 41 key-free operand swap 9d21a7fafac0e24f428e3c0124de5f8c54c1de8bef8535a636cfd97be5aad365 0583dc3e0351f69bc5 / ...6d83dc3e0351f69bad (2^30/2^30 both bfast, 0/2^30 non-bfast); len 48 class pair (words 2,3 swapped ^ T = 0x5b9234ff04f56f3d) 234/2^29 = 2^-21.13, class 2^43 seeds exactly.
per_hash.kind: key-free (eps = 1 for every seed and every 16-byte prefix, all four variants). For 17 <= len <= 32 the bytes beyond 16 enter only through G(u,v) = (lo(C2(C3^u)) ^ hi(C4(C5^v)), lo(C4(C5^v)) ^ hi(C2(C3^u))), a public function XORed into (i,j) after the seed terms, and every finalisation is a function of (i,j); read_short on the first 16 bytes is a bijection, so any two tails can be compensated in the prefix (construction A), or tails with G(t) = G(t') used with equal prefixes (2^36.1 solutions from the lattice identity C2*d = swap64(C4*delta), d = 0xb0e896630cf3a6b6, delta = 0x302997ce1c430f6d, or x' = x+2^62 / y' = y+1 with a carry-pattern condition; C2 = 0 mod 4). Score log2(17/8) = 1.1 bits (1.6 rounded to whole words), MUM tier. bfast variants additionally: key-free at 41..47 B (symmetric replace-by-product mumix on the untouched lane (s2,s5) = (C2^seed, C5^seed), swap through C2^C5) and weak-seed cosets of density exactly 2^-21 (lanes (s2,s3),(s4,s5)), 2^-22, 2^-23 at every length >= 33 with conditional rate 1.
per_hash.null_resolution: Generic differential scan (museair-foldscan): 6157 cells (complement, +-1, +-2^32, +2^63, single bits 0/31/32/63, byte +1/complement, paired same/opposite incl. all-ones on both operands, cross-length append/prepend/pad/truncate; lengths 1..40,48,63,64,65,96,128,160,200; random base) x 2^24 seeds and 30 cells x 2^30: 0 full collisions in all four variants and the low word of the 128-bit outputs, max per-bit |z| 4.96 (2^21 samples) / 3.72 (2^27); museair-hillclimb ~4.6-5.0e5 candidates per class (1..32, 33..95, 96..191, 192..400 B), top-20 null at 2^28, one 259-B pair null at 2^30; museair-weakseed short-path battery 44 pairs x 4 variants x 2^28: 0; non-bfast long path (>= 33 B): no route above the generic floor found (analysis; 26 swap pairs 0/2^28 random and 0/2^28 class-sampled; 60-B control 0/2^33) -- conjecture, not a proof; short path <= 16 B: seed -> (i,j) injective, best bfast-64 construction is 2 seeds (2^-63, proved); non-bfast nothing. bfast weak class seed = 0 mod 2^32 (eps 2^-32 at 60/64/80 B, exhaustive on the class) and the 2^-59 len-9 bfast-64 pair are claimed (museair-structure) but not independently verified and are dominated. Multi-seed z3: unknown at 600 s. Caveat: upstream master (v0.4 Jul 2025, v1/v2) changed the short path to (CONST ^ seed ^ u) * CONST; the break is against the SMHasher3-registered v0.3 only.
per_hash.provenance: Found independently by museair-structure (construction A, every length 17..32 at 2^20, len 17/32 at 2^30), museair-foldscan (lattice + carry-free search, len 32; also checked with SMHasher3's own museair.cpp), museair-hillclimb (carry-vector DP, len 32, k = 2..9), museair-smt (lattice + carry pattern DFS, len 32, 16 pairs) and komihash-smt (z3 on the hand-structured system, len 32, 2 pairs); bfast results by museair-weakseed and museair-structure. % ---- injective.tex, body paragraph after "\Cref{tab:injective:adversarial} gives the result": replace the komihash clause ----
%   old: "\texttt{komihash} resisted every differential we tried at $2^{32}$ seeds per surface, which bounds its score below only by our search effort."
%   new:
\texttt{komihash}, which resisted our complement search, loses to a
structural pair: for $64$--$127$-byte messages its four lane seeds are public
XOR offsets of two state words, and a fixed $64$-byte pair differing in two
bits collides for $91\%$ of all seeds ($3.1$ bits); \texttt{a5hash}'s
$64$-bit hash has a length-tunable weak-seed class ($47.8$ bits), while its
$128$-bit variants and every variant of \texttt{MuseAir} v0.3 have key-free
collisions at $17$ bytes.

% ---- appendix_adversarial.tex: replace the paragraph "\texttt{komihash} (random seed)." ----
\paragraph{\texttt{komihash} (random seed).}
\texttt{komihash} v5.34, re-implemented independently three times and checked
against its $63$ published test vectors and against the upstream header on
$2^{20}$ random inputs.  For $64$--$127$-byte messages the hash runs exactly one
iteration of its four-lane loop, whose lane seeds are \emph{public} XOR offsets
of the two state words, $\mathrm{Seed}_{k+1}=\mathrm{IVAL}_{k+1}\oplus S_1$ and
$\mathrm{Seed}_{k+5}=\mathrm{IVAL}_{k+5}\oplus S_5$, and whose exit combine XORs
the four $128$-bit lane products symmetrically except that each high half is
added to a different word $S_5\oplus\mathrm{IVAL}_{k+5}$.  Choosing
$w_1=w_0\oplus\mathrm{IVAL}_2\oplus1$ and $w_5=w_4\oplus\mathrm{IVAL}_6$ makes
lanes $0$ and $1$ compute $uv$ and $(u\oplus1)v$ with $u=w_0\oplus S_1$,
$v=w_4\oplus S_5$; flipping bit $0$ of $w_0$ and $w_1$ swaps the two products,
and the pair collides iff $(S_5+h_0)\oplus(S_6+h_1)=(S_5+h_1)\oplus(S_6+h_0)$
with $S_6=S_5\oplus\mathrm{IVAL}_6$ and $h_k$ the high halves.  Since
$(u\oplus1)v=uv\pm v$, $h_1-h_0\in\{0,\pm1\}$: the collision is certain when the
low word does not carry (probability $1-\mathbb E[v]/2^{64}$) and otherwise
holds with probability exactly $3/4$ ($\mathrm{IVAL}_6$ ends in binary
$\ldots1100$).  The preseeded $S_5=B+\mathrm{hi}(AB)$ is skewed (bit $63$ set
with probability $0.281$, because $A$ and $B$ carry only the even, resp.\ odd,
seed bits), so $w_4=\texttt{0x5e8}\ll52$ brings $\mathbb E[v]/2^{64}$ down to
$0.357$ and the rate up to $1-0.357/4=0.911$.  The pair
$m=\texttt{c1675e0bb980a575 84142e08970abc66 63f1ee08469ccdac 9ff735ab278a84ba
000000000000805e 6c0ce934cf66d4e0 737a74e5f8908faf afcc5252147fbc5b}$ (bytes,
little-endian words) and $m'=m$ with bit $0$ of bytes $0$ and $8$ flipped
collides with probability $0.9106=2^{-0.135}$: $244{,}431{,}875$ and
$244{,}434{,}592$ of $2^{28}$ seeds in two independent re-implementations,
$61{,}112{,}879$ of $2^{26}$ through the upstream header, and the carry
predicate above coincided with the collision on every one of $2^{29}$ seeds.
The rate is identical at every length $64$--$127$ (any common suffix) and $0$
in $2^{28}$ at $63$, $128$ and $192$ bytes, where the lane words lose their
public relation.  Placing the flipped bit on the second operand instead gives
exactly $7/8$ ($939{,}508{,}211$ of $2^{30}$) and lanes $(2,3)$ give $3/4$.
Hence $\varepsilon=0.911$ at $L=8$ and \texttt{komihash} scores $3.1$ bits: not
key-free ($9\%$ of seeds separate the pair) but far below the $2^{-27}$ tier.
Nothing else was found: word-level additive, single-bit and byte differentials
at every position of lengths $1$--$200$ ($4910$ cells at $2^{24}$ seeds, $115$
at $2^{30}$), $7008$ structured pairs at lengths $1$--$63$ ($2^{23}$ seeds
each), an evolutionary search (best pairs re-measured at $2^{28}$) and the
earlier $2^{32}$ complement scan all gave $0$ collisions.  The hash has no
public-only path (every message word meets a seeded word before any multiply),
and its seed-expanded word $S_5$ is never $0$, $1$, $2^{63}$ or $2^{64}-1$
(exact enumeration of all $2^{64}$ seeds); its densest value is hit by $268$
seeds, a dead-multiplier class at $2^{-55.9}$ that the lane swap makes
irrelevant.

% ---- appendix_adversarial.tex: new paragraphs (after MUM) ----
\paragraph{\texttt{a5hash} v5.21 (random seed).}
Re-implemented from SMHasher3's \texttt{a5hash.cpp} and checked against its
three registered verification values (\texttt{ADDE79B3}, \texttt{89406B11},
\texttt{14AD402C}).  The $64$-bit hash has no public-only path, and a
differential scan of $4873$ cells (complements, $\pm1$, $\pm2^{32}$, $2^{63}$,
single bits, byte increments, paired and cross-length differences at lengths
$1$--$200$) at $2^{24}$ seeds, $143$ structured pairs at $2^{26}$ and an
evolutionary search re-measured at $2^{28}$ found nothing.  Its weakness is the
seed expansion: the initial state is $(\mathrm{lo},\mathrm{hi})(XY)$ with
$X=K_2\oplus\ell\oplus(\mathrm{seed}\,\&\,\texttt{0xAA}\cdots)$ and
$Y=K_1\oplus\ell\oplus(\mathrm{seed}\,\&\,\texttt{0x55}\cdots)$, so the even
bit positions of $X$ and the odd ones of $Y$ are fixed by the length $\ell$,
and $v_2(\mathrm{lo}(XY))=v_2(X)+v_2(Y)$ is chosen through $\ell$ (as a
by-product, $\mathrm{hi}(XY)$ has bit $63=0$ for every seed and
$\mathrm{lo}(XY)$ is even for every odd length).  At $\ell=6615$ the value
$W^*=\texttt{0x8e5caae000000000}$ costs $19$ seed bits for the valuations
$(20,17)$ and a $27$-bit residual product that $118$ of the $2^{26}$ remaining
relevant assignments satisfy, so $\Pr[\mathrm{Seed}_1=W^*]=118\cdot2^{-45}
=2^{-38.1}$ exactly (complete enumeration, reproduced independently).  A
message whose first block word is $W^*$ then multiplies by zero and its second
word is dead: $m=\texttt{e0aa5c8e00000000\,8877665544332211}\,\|\,F$ and
$m'=\texttt{e0aa5c8e00000000\,1122334455667788}\,\|\,F$ (any common
$6599$-byte $F$) collide on every one of the $118\cdot2^{19}$ class seeds and
on none of $2^{30}+2^{28}$ random control seeds; uniform sampling inside the
$2^{-19}$ valuation stratum gave $1821$ collisions in $2^{30}$ against
$1888\pm44$ predicted.  With $L=827$ words this is $47.8$ bits, the minimum
over the lengths we enumerated ($51.2$ at $15$ bytes, an exact fibre of
$13136$ seeds; $51.3$ at $137{,}687$ bytes; $52.9$ at $15.9$\,MB, where
$\varepsilon=2^{-32}$ exactly); shorter or better lengths may exist.  The
$128$-bit variants \texttt{a5hash\_128} and \texttt{a5hash\_128\_\_64} are
broken key-free: their extra state words
$\mathrm{Seed}_3=\texttt{0xA4093822299F31D0}$,
$\mathrm{Seed}_4=\texttt{0xC0AC29B7C97C50DD}$ (and $\mathrm{Seed}_5$--$8$) are
unseeded constants, so for $17$--$32$ bytes the product
$(c+\mathrm{Seed}_3)(d+\mathrm{Seed}_4)$ of the last two words is public,
$c=-\mathrm{Seed}_3$ zeroes it and $d$ is free ($2^{64}$-way collisions; the
same at $33$--$64$ bytes and in three lanes of every first $64$-byte block
beyond).  The $17$-byte pair $\texttt{00ddc7f65b30ce60d6}\,\texttt{00}^{8}$
versus the same with last byte \texttt{ff} collides for every seed ($2^{20}$
seeds; $24$- and $32$-byte pairs at $2^{30}$), i.e.\ $1.1$ bits at $L=17/8$
($1.6$ if lengths are rounded up to whole words), the \texttt{MUM} tier; the
$64$-bit hash does not collide on these pairs.

\paragraph{\texttt{MuseAir} v0.3.}
SMHasher3's \texttt{museair.cpp} (all four variants; verification values
\texttt{F89F1683}, \texttt{C61BEE56}, \texttt{D3DFE238}, \texttt{27939BF1}
reproduced by five independent re-implementations).  For $17$--$32$ bytes the
short path reads the first $16$ bytes into $(i,j)$ (a bijection), adds the
seed through $(\mathrm{lo},\mathrm{hi})((\mathrm{seed}\oplus C_0)(\ell\oplus
C_1))$, and then XORs in
$G(u,v)=(\mathrm{lo}(C_2(C_3\oplus u))\oplus\mathrm{hi}(C_4(C_5\oplus v)),\
\mathrm{lo}(C_4(C_5\oplus v))\oplus\mathrm{hi}(C_2(C_3\oplus u)))$, a
\emph{public} function of the remaining bytes; every finalisation is a function
of $(i,j)$.  Two distinct tails $t,t'$ whose prefixes satisfy
$\mathrm{read}(p')=\mathrm{read}(p)\oplus G(t)\oplus G(t')$ therefore collide
for every seed at every length $17$--$32$: the $17$-byte pair
$\texttt{95035294f2065da4d5aebfbee6b7dcf275}$,
$\texttt{f966f58b6a8749a4726e03c846fee90b1d}$ collided on all $2^{30}$ seeds
tried in all four variants.  Equal prefixes work as well: $G(t)=G(t')$ has
about $2^{36}$ solutions, from the lattice identity $C_2\,d=\mathrm{swap}_{64}
(C_4\,\delta)$ with $d=\texttt{0xb0e896630cf3a6b6}$,
$\delta=\texttt{0x302997ce1c430f6d}$, or from $x'=x+2^{62}$, $y'=y+1$ with a
carry-pattern condition ($C_2\equiv0\bmod4$); four such $32$-byte pairs, found
by four independent searches, each collide on $2^{28}$--$2^{30}$ seeds, one
also through SMHasher3's own source.  \texttt{MuseAir} v0.3 thus scores $1.1$
bits (the \texttt{MUM} tier) in every variant.  The \texttt{bfast} variants
replace their state by the $128$-bit product in the mixing step, which is
symmetric in its operands: swapping the last two words through the public
constant $C_2\oplus C_5$ collides key-free at $41$--$47$ bytes ($2^{30}/2^{30}$;
$0$ for the non-\texttt{bfast} variants), and at $\ge48$ bytes swapping words
$2,3$ XORed with $T=\texttt{0x5b9234ff04f56f3d}$ collides on the coset
$(C_2\oplus\mathrm{seed})\oplus(C_3+\mathrm{seed})=T$ of exactly $2^{43}$ seeds
($234$ hits in $2^{29}$, $2^{-21.1}$).  A differential scan ($6157$ cells at
$2^{24}$, $30$ at $2^{30}$) and an evolutionary search found nothing beyond
these, and the non-\texttt{bfast} long path ($\ge33$ bytes) gave no route above
the generic floor.  Upstream has since replaced the short path (v0.4 and v2
multiply $C\oplus\mathrm{seed}\oplus u$ by a constant), which we did not
analyse.

% ---- appendix_adversarial.tex, "A seeded-differential test for SMHasher3": add after "show no collision in $2^{30}$ seeds." ----
The test's pair family is complement-based and therefore blind to the
structural pairs above (\texttt{komihash} and \texttt{a5hash} pass it); the
lane-swap, dead-operand and public-product families should be added to it.

% ---- Caveat paragraph: add a sentence ----
The \texttt{komihash}, \texttt{a5hash} and \texttt{MuseAir} entries come from
structural analysis of the source rather than the differential scan; their
rates are exact (key-free pairs, enumerated seed classes) or measured to
$\pm10^{-4}$ ($2^{28}$--$2^{30}$ seeds, two independent re-implementations
each), and each was reproduced by an independent verifier before being
recorded here.

% Provenance: all code and logs in experiment/deep/<hash>-<method>/ and verify-<hash>-<method>/ (README.md with exact commands); to be ported into tools/bench/adversarial/ (selftest.cpp cases, MANIFEST entries) before the arXiv bundle.
discarded: All multi-seed z3 queries (komihash-smt, a5hash-smt, museair-smt: K = 1..3 hard-coded seeds, symbolic pairs, seed classes): every instance returned 'unknown' at 100-600 s (one trivial len-1 UNSAT); they carry no information for or against any hash and are not cited as coverage.

The three evolutionary/hill-climb searches (komihash, a5hash, MuseAir) as evidence of security: their objectives (partial collisions, per-bit bias) have no gradient through the seed-dependent finalisations; their top pairs are null at 2^28 and their coverage (~2^22-2^23 local mutants) is negligible. The effects those agents reported came from structural analysis seeded by hand, not from the search.

The generic foldscan null results as evidence against the structural attacks: scans on a random base cannot reach pairs that need a structured base (komihash's w1 = w0^IVAL2, a5hash's W0 = W*, MuseAir's compensated prefix), which is exactly why three scans missed three breaks. Retained only as coverage statements for their own difference families (< 2^-22.4 at 2^24, < 2^-28.4 at 2^30 per cell).

komihash-hillclimb's plain lane-swap rows (~2^-26 at 2^30, lanes 1<->3 and 2<->3) and its laneswap_0k rows (wrong lane-0 offset, void by the agent's own admission): superseded by the equal-multiplier pair; its verifier's wording 'key-free trail at rate 3/4' is wrong terminology (a 3/4-rate pair is not key-free) and is not adopted.

komihash-weakseed's S5'-neutralisation class (T = 0x7d438b0c00003c62, 268 preimages, 2^-55.9) and its conjecture that the true maximum is 'well above 2^-56' (uint8 counters saturated; only one dense prefix enumerated): not independently verified and immaterial for the score (eps = 0.91 dominates); the seed-0 class (5 seeds incl. the default seed) is outside the random-seed model.

komihash-structure's conjecture that 0.9106 is the family optimum and its 'proved' status for the exact 7/8 and 3/4 constants (derived under a uniformity assumption, confirmed to four digits only): kept as measured, not proved; also its crosscheck line quoting the untuned pair's hash for the tuned pair (verifier caught it).

a5hash-smt's headline '57.7 bits proven / ~53 conjectured' and its ~2^-52 union estimate (unmeasured density between 24 and 64 bits of resolution): superseded by the exact len-6615 class (47.8 bits); its len-24 density '2^-57 (conjecture)' was corrected by the verifier to exactly 104 seeds = 2^-57.30, immaterial.

a5hash-weakseed's hi(x*y) = 0 class extrapolation (~2^-54 at 64 bits from relaxed events) and its tool's printed 'model class density 2^-52.5' (the agent itself says not to quote it); its a5hash_32 exhaustive results (a different, 32-bit-seed hash, not scored).

a5hash-foldscan's greedy (beam width 1) weak-seed lower bounds (2^-53.5 at 17 B, 2^-54.6 at 32 B) and a5hash-structure's conjecture that len 15 gives ~48-51 bits: superseded by the exact fibres (len 15: 13136 seeds, 51.2 bits; len 16: 5626) and by the len-6615 pair.

MuseAir construction C (seed = 0 mod 2^32, eps = 2^-32 at 60/64/80 B, bfast) and construction D (32-seed class, 2^-59 at 9 B, bfast-64): not independently verified (C's 2^32-class exhaustive check is the claimant's only) and dominated by the key-free pairs; museair-weakseed's 2-seed short-path pair (2^-63) is at the floor.

The original MuseAir lead's details (C2 odd; a 2^63 XOR difference in hi(C4*y)): wrong, as three agents showed (C2 = 0x7ab1006b26f9eb64 is divisible by 4; hi(C4*y) < C4 < 2^59). The working differentials are x' = x+2^62 (lo(C2 x) unchanged) with y' = y+1 and a carry-pattern condition, or the exact lattice identity C2*d = swap64(C4*delta).

Note-level slips not propagated: museair-hillclimb's 'v'-v = 3' (actually 19) in the komihash-smt pair; museair-smt/hillclimb's 'bits = 2 at L = 4 words' (superseded by the 17-byte pair at L = 17/8 and the paper's key-free convention); the agents' claim that all lengths 17..32 (MuseAir) and every length >= 17 (a5hash-128) were verified: only 17, 24, 32 (a5hash-128) and 17, 32, 41, 48 (MuseAir) have independent verification, the rest rests on the source-level proof plus the claimants' 2^16-2^20 runs.

The komihash-structure/weakseed bias claims at 2^30/2^32 on the preseeded S1 ('flat') and on S5' low bits: measured by the claimants only; the S5 bit-63 skew (0.281) was re-measured by a verifier and is the only bias figure used.

res.method: Structural inventory of every message-to-state contact in komihash.h v5.34 (all branches of komihash_inner, komihash_epi, HASHLOOP64), enumeration of the length classes and overlapping-read patterns, then constructions from the one public state relation that exists: in the 64-byte loop the lane seeds are Seed2..4 = IVAL2..4 ^ S1 and Seed6..8 = IVAL6..8 ^ S5 (public XOR offsets), and the exit combine S1 ^= S2^S3^S4, S5 ^= S6^S7^S8 is XOR-symmetric in the lanes. For a one-iteration message (64 <= len <= 127) the epilogue sees only S5_out = XOR_k ((S5^IVY_k) + hi(P_k)) and S1_out = XOR_k lo(P_k) ^ S5_out, so a pair whose effective lane words are permuted (x'_k = x_pi(k), y'_k = y_pi(k) with x_k = m_k ^ IVX_k, y_k = m_{4+k} ^ IVY_k) collides iff the hi halves survive the permutation under the lane-specific additions. Making lanes 0 and 1 differ by one low bit (y_1 = y_0 ^ 1) gives P_1 = P_0 +- u, so hi(P_1) - hi(P_0) in {0,+1,-1}, and the carry condition then holds with probability 1 / 3/4 / 3/4. The swapped message differs from the original in exactly 2 bits. Tuning: with the bit on the x side the product difference is v = y ^ S5, and the preseeded S5 = B + hi(A*B) is heavily skewed (bit 63 set w.p. 0.281), so the filler y = 0x5ea<<52 minimising E[y^S5] raises eps to 0.911. All rates measured at 2^26 uniformly random seeds (splitmix64 of a counter), 3 threads locally; a due-diligence scan of 7008 structured single-byte/word differences over every non-loop length 1..63 ran on the 96-core server at 2^20 and 2^23 seeds (16 threads). Preseed-state per-bit bias at 2^30 seeds.
res.validated_against: Own single-file implementation komi_ref.h: 63/63 published README test vectors (the table in the vendored selftest.cpp: 5 strings + 17 bulk lengths for seeds 0, 0x0123456789abcdef, 256) and 0 mismatches against the vendored komihash.h on 2^20 random (message, length 0..300, seed) triples. The main pair was additionally re-evaluated with the vendored komihash.h directly (crosscheck.cpp): 916846/2^20 collisions and H(M)=H(M')=0xdbaa78e2b55f6dfd at seed 0x3ec66ecfa0d53022.
res.summary: komihash v5.34 is broken for message lengths 64..127 bytes: a 64-byte pair differing in 2 bits (bit 0 of words 4 and 5) collides for 87.5% of seeds (58717690 of 2^26), and a tuned pair collides for 91.06% (61110213 of 2^26). Mechanism: the first (and, for len<=127, only) HASHLOOP64 iteration uses lane seeds that are public XOR offsets of the same two words, and the exit combine is XOR-symmetric, so swapping two lanes through the public IVAL offsets permutes the products; the only asymmetry is that hi halves are ADDED to different words S5^IVAL_k, and a one-bit difference between the two lanes keeps the hi halves equal or +-1, which the carry condition absorbs with probability 1/2 + 1/2*3/4 = 7/8. The exact condition (S5+h0)^(S6+h1)==(S5+h1)^(S6+h0) predicts the collision on 1048576/1048576 checked seeds. Filler tuning exploits a second finding: the preseeded S5 is strongly skewed (bit 63 set with probability 0.281, z=-14326 at 2^30; top nibbles 0xb/0xc never occur), because S5 = B + hi(A*B) with A,B confined to fixed ranges by the even/odd seed-bit split. Score: bits = log2(8 words / 0.9106) = 3.1. No key-free (every-seed) pair exists: every message byte is XORed with seed-dependent state before any multiply, so there is no public-only path; the tail encodings are injective with length markers and no overlapping read reuses a byte. Structured additive/complement differences on all lengths 1..63 (7008 pairs, 2^23 seeds each) gave 0 collisions; lengths >=128 break the public lane relation (0 in 2^26).

pairs.conditional_on: C1: (S5+h0)^(S6+h1) == (S5+h1)^(S6+h0) with h_k = hi(lane-k product), S6 = S5^IVAL6; holds iff h1==h0 (prob ~1/2) or h1==h0+-1 and bits 0,1 of (S5+h0) pass the carry test (3/4)
pairs.notes: Main construction: lanes 0,1 of the first 64-byte block swapped through the public offsets IVAL2/IVAL6 with y_1 = y_0 ^ 1 (m1 = m0 ^ IVAL2, m5 = m4 ^ IVAL6 ^ 1); M' = M with bit 0 of words 4 and 5 flipped (Hamming distance 2). Rate 0.874962 = 7/8. Same rate at lengths 65, 100, 127 with a common suffix (58717690/2^26 each); 0/2^26 at length 128. Vendored komihash.h reproduces 916846/2^20 and the example seed.

pairs.conditional_on: same C1 with the +-v difference on the x side (x_1 = x_0 ^ 1): v = y^S5, and y = 0x5ea<<52 chosen to minimise E[y ^ S5] over the skewed preseeded S5 (E[v/2^64] = 0.358)
pairs.notes: Tuned construction: predicted 3/4 + (1-0.358)/4 = 0.9106, measured 0.910613. Bits score log2(8/0.9106) = 3.1. Untuned x-side with an arbitrary filler measured 0.8417 (the same skew working against the attacker).

Lane pair (2,3): IVAL7^IVAL8 = ..CA agrees with S5 on bit 0 only, predicted 3/4, measured 0.749987. Lane pairs (0,2),(0,3),(1,2),(1,3) (offset XOR odd) predicted 1/2, measured 0.499948/0.499948/0.500078/0.500078 (33550949, 33550949, 33559648, 33559648 of 2^26). Lanes (0,1) with bit 1 instead of bit 0: 0.749997; with bit 63: 0/2^26.

pairs.m2_hex: (lanes 0,1 swapped through public offsets, no one-bit trick)

Preseeded S5 = B + hi(A*B) (A = IVAL1^(seed&0x55..) in [2^61,2^63), B = IVAL5^(seed&0xAA..) in [2^62,2^63) u [3*2^62,2^64)): bit 63 is 1 with probability 0.2814 (z=-14326), bit 62 0.5722 (z=+4732), bit 61 0.4218 (z=-5127), bit 60 0.5575; 27 bits (37..63) have |z|>=6; top nibbles 0xb and 0xc never occur, 0x5 has frequency 0.152. claims.claim: For 64 <= len <= 127 the epilogue depends on the loop only through S5_out = XOR_k ((S5^IVY_k) + hi(P_k)) and S1_out = XOR_k lo(P_k) ^ S5_out, where P_k = (m_k ^ IVX_k ^ S1)(m_{4+k} ^ IVY_k ^ S5), IVX = (0,IVAL2,IVAL3,IVAL4), IVY = (0,IVAL6,IVAL7,IVAL8); hence any pair whose effective lane words are permuted collides iff the permuted hi-half sum equals the original.
claims.evidence: Direct expansion of HASHLOOP64 (komihash.h lines 727-756) and the exit combine (lines 939-940) for one iteration; the lane seeds are set at lines 930-935. Checked on 2^20 seeds by algcheck.cpp (C1 <=> H(M)==H(M') on 1048576/1048576).

claims.claim: With x_1 = x_0 and y_1 = y_0 ^ 1 the lane products satisfy P_1 = P_0 +- u (u = x_0 ^ S1), so hi(P_1) - hi(P_0) in {0,+1,-1}; the collision condition then reduces to: always if equal, and to 'bits 0,1 of (S5+h0) not both 1' (resp. 'not both 0') for +1 (resp. -1), because IVAL6 = 0xBE5466CF34E90C6C has bits 0,1 = 00 and bit 2 = 1. Total probability 1/2 + 1/2 * 3/4 = 7/8 under uniform low bits.
claims.evidence: (w+1)^w = 2^(t+1)-1 with t = trailing ones; a=S5 and b=S5^IVAL6 share bits 0,1 and differ at bit 2. Fine-grained prediction verified on 1048576/1048576 seeds (algcheck.log: h1==h0 524388 all collide; h1==h0+1 261274 with 0.7496 colliding; h1==h0-1 262914 with 0.7512).

claims.claim: Main 64-byte pair (2-bit difference) collides with probability 0.874962; tuned pair with probability 0.910613; both carry over unchanged to every length 65..127 with a common suffix.
claims.evidence: 2^26 uniformly random seeds each (variants.log, opty.log): 58717690 and 61110213 collisions; lengths 65/100/127 give 58717690 each; length 128 gives 0; vendored komihash.h reproduces 916846/2^20 for the main pair (crosscheck.log).

claims.claim: The preseeded S5 is skewed: bit 63 set with probability 0.2814 (z = -14326 at 2^30 seeds), 27 bits with |z| >= 6, top nibbles 0xb/0xc never occur; preseeded S1 is unbiased (max |z| 2.6).
claims.evidence: initbias.log, 2^30 seeds. Explained by S5 = B + hi(A*B) with A in [2^61,2^63) and B in [2^62,2^63) u [3*2^62,2^64) fixed by the even/odd seed-bit split and IVAL1/IVAL5 top bits.

claims.claim: komihash has no public-only path: every message byte is XORed with S1 or S5 (seed-dependent) before any multiply, in every length class; tail encodings are injective with a length-marker bit and no overlapping read reuses a byte (shifted out). Therefore no seed-independent (key-free) collision exists for any pair, and cross-length pairs cannot equalise the pre-HASHFIN input.
claims.evidence: Inspection of every branch of komihash_inner (lines 831-897), komihash_epi (767-806) and HASHLOOP64 (727-756); the length-class table in README.md lists each encoding.

claims.claim: No pair in the lane-swap family collides for every seed: hi((x^S1)(y^S5)) == hi((x'^S1)(y'^S5)) for all (S1,S5) is impossible for (x,y) != (x',y'), so eps < 1; the maximum found is 0.9106.
claims.evidence: Argument: the product difference is a nonzero integer multiple of a seed-dependent word and crosses the 2^64 boundary for a constant fraction of seeds; the tuned rate is bounded by 3/4 + (1 - min_y E[(y^S5)/2^64])/4 = 0.9106 for the (0,1) lane pair (E computed from the empirical S5 histogram). Not exhaustively proved; other permutations or a joint tuning of low bits were not explored.

claims.claim: Structured additive/complement single-byte and word differences at every position of every non-loop length 1..63 give no collisions above the 2^-64 floor.
claims.evidence: 7008 pairs x 2^20 seeds and 7008 pairs x 2^23 seeds: 0 collisions (scan_short_2p20.log, scan_short_2p23.log).

res.method: Weak-seed classes and seed-expansion structure. (1) Wrote an independent single-file implementation (kh.h) from a read of the vendored komihash.h and validated it against the 63 published README vectors plus a 2^20-input random cross-check against the vendored reference (0 mismatches). (2) Expressed both operands of every multiply as functions of (seed, message): preseed HASHROUND (S1_0 = IVAL1^(seed&0x55..), S5_0 = IVAL5^(seed&0xAA..), 32 seed bits each, S5_0 always odd, hi(S1_0*S5_0) < 2^63), HASH16 blocks (m0^S1)(m1^S5), the 64-byte lane loop where lane k multiplies (w[k-1]^IVAL_k^S1') by (w[3+k]^IVAL_{4+k}^S5') with PUBLIC XOR offsets and the exit combine XORs all four lane products symmetrically (S1 = lo1^lo2^lo3^lo4^T, S5 = T, T = (S5'+h1)^(IVAL6^S5'+h2)^(IVAL7^S5'+h3)^(IVAL8^S5'+h4)), and the tails (r2h = S5' bare for len<8). (3) Measured the distribution of S1' and S5' over 2^32 random seeds (per-bit z-scores, 16/24/32-bit windows, min-entropy). (4) Built an exact enumerator of the preimage count of S5' = T over ALL 2^64 seeds (for fixed odd-bit word B the map A -> hi(A*B) is monotone, so the A's hitting a target strip lie in one interval whose even-bit-coset members are enumerated; every (A,B) re-verified with the preseed function) and ran it on structured targets, on the seed-0 value, and on the whole 2^32-target strip under the densest top-32 prefix. (5) Constructed the lane-swap message pair implied by the public lane offsets and the XOR-symmetric exit combine, derived its exact collision predicate, verified the predicate against the reference hash on 4x2^22 seeds, decomposed the rate, optimised the attacker-chosen word w4 against the measured S5' skew, and measured the rate on the server at 2^28 seeds for lane pairs (1,2),(1,3),(3,4), differences dx/dy, and lengths 63..128. (6) Verified the S5'-neutralisation pairs on their exhaustively enumerated preimage seed sets.
res.validated_against: Own implementation kh.h: 63/63 published komihash README test vectors (seeds 0, 0x0123456789ABCDEF, 256; 5 strings + bulk lengths 3..256) and 0 mismatches vs the vendored komihash.h v5.34 on 2^20 random (len<=300, seed) inputs (kh_selftest.c, run locally and on the server: out_selftest.txt). All collision counts were taken with the VENDORED reference; every hit was cross-checked with the own implementation (ownimpl_mismatch=0 in every run).
res.summary: komihash is broken at 64..127-byte messages: a fixed two-bit-difference pair collides for 91% of all seeds (eps = 0.9106 measured at 2^28 seeds; bits = log2(8/0.9106) = 3.14). Mechanism: for one 64-byte loop iteration the four lane seeds are public XOR offsets (IVAL2..4, IVAL6..8) of the two seed words, so a message whose lane-2 words equal its lane-1 words XOR (IVAL2^1, IVAL6), paired with the same message with bit 0 flipped in words 0 and 1, makes lanes 1 and 2 compute the SAME two products in swapped order for EVERY seed; the exit combine is XOR-symmetric in the lo halves, so the only residual condition is (S5'+h1)^(IVAL6^S5'+h2) == (S5'+h2)^(IVAL6^S5'+h1) with h2-h1 = carry of one addition, which holds when there is no carry (Pr = 1-E[w4^S5']/2^64 = 0.64 with w4 chosen against the measured S5' skew) or, otherwise, when the two trailing bits of S5'+h1 are not both set (Pr = 3/4 exactly, because IVAL6 ends in ...00). Predicate verified == reference collision on 4x2^22 seeds. Fails at len<=63 (no lanes) and len>=128 (second block consumes the individual lane words). Second finding (weak-seed class): the seed-expansion word S5' = S5_0 + hi(S1_0*S5_0) is strongly non-uniform in its top bits (bit 63 has Pr[1] = 0.281, z = -28657 at 2^32; top nibble never 0xB/0xC; top-16 min-entropy 12.24 bits; top-32 min-entropy <= 25.3 bits), and exact enumeration over all 2^64 seeds shows the densest top-32 strip holds 450,234,633,598 seeds (105x uniform) with >= 71.9 million 64-bit targets T having >= 255 preimage seeds; T = 0x7d438b0c00003c62 has exactly 268, so the first HASH16 block's second operand m1^S5' is zero for 2^-55.9 of seeds when m1 = T, neutralising m0 (32-byte pair verified colliding on all 268 preimage seeds). S1' shows no measurable bias. S5' = 0 has no preimage (the bare-seed tail multiply never degenerates).

res.validated_against: Own single-file implementation kh.h validated against the 63 published README vectors (seeds 0, 0x0123456789ABCDEF, 256; strings + bulk lengths; 63/63 match) and cross-checked against the vendored komihash.h v5.34 on 200000 random (len 0..300, seed, message) triples (200000/200000 agree). The headline pair was additionally measured by calling the vendored komihash.h directly (equal_u_vendored.cpp, 2^20 seeds).
res.summary: komihash v5.34 is broken for every message length 64..127 bytes: a fixed 64-byte pair differing in two bits collides for 7/8 of all seeds (measured 234876389 / 2^28 = 0.87498, 2^-0.19; predicted exactly 7/8), so bits = log2(8 / 0.875) = 3.2. Mechanism: in the one-block path the four lane products use seeds Seed_k = A_k ^ Seed1, Seed_{4+k} = B_k ^ Seed5 with PUBLIC constants A = (0, IVAL2, IVAL3, IVAL4), B = (0, IVAL6, IVAL7, IVAL8), and the exit combine is S1f = (lo0^lo1^lo2^lo3) ^ S5f, S5f = (s5+hi0)^(s6+hi1)^(s7+hi2)^(s8+hi3), symmetric under permuting lanes. Choose w_k = w_j ^ A_j ^ A_k (lanes j,k share the multiplier u) and w_{4+k} = w_{4+j} ^ B_j ^ B_k ^ 1 (second operands v and v^1); m' flips bit 0 of both w_{4+j} and w_{4+k}, which is exactly the lane swap. u*(v^1) = u*v +/- u, so hi64 is unchanged with probability 1/2 (no carry out of the low word) and then the entire state is identical; when hi changes by 1 the residual carry-difference condition holds with a further 1/2*(1-2^-t), t = lowest set bit of B_j^B_k: eps = 7/8 for lanes 0<->1 (t=2), 3/4 for 2<->3 (t=1), 1/2 for the other four lane pairs -- all measured to 4 digits at 2^28 seeds. Controls: the same pair at len 63 and 128 gives 0 collisions at 2^18. A plain lane swap without the equal-u relation still collides at 2^-26.1 (lanes 1<->3: 15 hits at 2^30). The evolutionary search itself found nothing: its top-5 pairs are null at 2^28 (max |z| 3.55 over 128 tests, no partial-collision excess).

res.method: Multi-seed SMT (z3 4.15.4) on exact 64-bit bit-vector models of the short paths (komihash len 0..31, a5hash len 0..32, MuseAir short path len 0..32), plus a seed-eliminated key-free system for MuseAir 17..32 B. The generic multi-seed queries (K hard-coded seeds, variable x variable 64x64 products) all timed out; the MuseAir key-free system was solved by hand-structuring the difference (x' = x + 2^62 so that lo(C2*x) is unchanged because 4 | C2; y' = y + 1 so that hi(C4*y) is unchanged when no carry) and letting z3 solve the remaining carry-pattern equation a^(a+C2/4) == b^(b+C4) in 19 s. Each SAT model was packed into a 32-byte message pair and measured in C over 2^24 random seeds (splitmix64), also with a random 16-byte prefix per trial.
res.validated_against: komihash_my vs the vendored komihash.h 5.34: 0 mismatches on 200000 random (seed, message, len 0..299) cases + README vectors (seed 0 32-byte string 05ad960802903a9d, seed 0x0123456789abcdef '7 chars' 90ab7c9f831cd940). a5hash_my and museair_my reproduce the SMHasher3 _ComputedVerifyImpl codes exactly: ADDE79B3 (a5hash), F89F1683 (MuseAir), C61BEE56 (bfast), D3DFE238 (MuseAir_128), 27939BF1 (128 bfast). z3 models vs the C oracle: 2004 checks, len 0..31, all 6 functions, 0 mismatches.
res.summary: FOUND: a key-free collision family for MuseAir v0.3 at 32 bytes that collides for EVERY seed and EVERY common 16-byte prefix, for all four variants (64, bfast, 128, 128-bfast): eps = 1, so MuseAir scores 0 bits in the paper's metric (like MUM). Mechanism: bytes 16..32 enter the short path only through the public products C2*(C3^u) and C4*(C5^v); since C2 = 0x7ab1006b26f9eb64 is divisible by 4, adding 2^62 to x = C3^u leaves lo(C2 x) unchanged and adds C2/4 to hi(C2 x); adding 1 to y = C5^v adds C4 to lo(C4 y) and leaves hi(C4 y) unchanged when no carry; the collision then reduces to the carry-pattern equation hi(C2 x) ^ (hi(C2 x)+C2/4) == lo(C4 y) ^ (lo(C4 y)+C4), which has 2^36.13 solutions (exact carry-vector DP count). Two explicit pairs measured: 16777216/16777216 collisions at 2^24 random seeds, also 16777216/16777216 with a random prefix per trial, for all four variants; control pair 0/2^20. Not found: no multi-seed collision for komihash (len 15, 31) or a5hash (len 16) or MuseAir <= 16 B — all z3 queries with K=2 hard-coded seeds returned unknown at 100-300 s (variable x variable products are beyond bit-blasting in the time box); K=3,4, symbolic seed classes and one-word/one-byte restrictions were not reached. Key-free MuseAir at lengths 24 and 28 with <= 2 differing bytes: several single-byte positions proved UNSAT at len 28, the rest unknown; lengths 17..23, 25..27, 29..31 not run.

(2) The key-free family is proved and measured only at length 32 (where u and v are independent 64-bit words); at lengths 17..31 the overlapping read_short windows tie u and v and no collision was found in the small time-boxed z3 sweeps (a few len-28 single-byte classes proved UNSAT, most classes unknown; lengths 17..23, 25..27, 29..31 not run). Since the paper's score takes the min over lengths, the length-32 family already gives eps=1. (3) All komihash / a5hash results are 'unknown' timeouts: z3 does not bit-blast variable x variable 64x64 products within 100-300 s, so nothing is proved or refuted for them; the planned K=3,4, symbolic-seed-class, and one-word/one-byte restricted queries did not run in the 50-minute budget. (4) No server run was used; all measurements are local (2^24 trials, one splitmix64 stream, fixed seed 12345 / 777). (5) Not covered: MuseAir long path (>32 B), a5hash 128-bit variants, komihash >=64 B lane structure.

res.hash: a5hash (SMHasher3 hashes/a5hash.cpp, v5.21: a5hash 64-bit, a5hash_128, a5hash_128__64; upstream v5.25 has the same structure)
res.method: Structure analysis and key-free / weak-seed constructions. (1) Transcribed a5hash64 and a5hash128 into a single header (a5.h) and validated it by reproducing SMHasher3's verification procedure. (2) Wrote down every place a message word meets the state per length class (0, 1-3, 4-7, 8-15, 16, >16 blocks+tail) and the overlapping 32-bit read patterns; the 64-bit hash has no public-only path (state = (lo,hi)(X*Y) with X carrying only the odd seed bits and Y only the even seed bits). (3) 128-bit variants: Seed3/Seed4 (and Seed5..8) are constants, so for len>=17 message words pass through PUBLIC 128-bit products (c+K3)(d+K4) etc.; built 12 explicit key-free pairs (dead operand u=0, swap, (2u,v/2), 3*5=15*1, 7*9=21*3, 11*13=143*1; lengths 17,24,32,48,64,100,200) and verified on 2^20 random seeds each (full 128-bit output; also the truncated-64 variant; control: same pair on the 64-bit hash gives 0). (4) 64-bit hash: v2(Seed1_init)=v2(X)+v2(Y); choosing len so that the fixed (K^len) bits vanish makes Pr[Seed1_init = W*] >> 2^-64 (search_len.py); enum_mode.c computes Pr[Seed1_init=W*] EXACTLY by enumerating every relevant seed bit (histogram of the residual product), then verifies that every conforming seed (fixed bits + enumerated bits + random upper bits) gives a full a5hash64 collision for the pair W0=W*, W1 != W1' (first block dead); control on random seeds. (5) Per-bit bias of the initial state at 2^30 seeds for 14 lengths. (6) 143 structured pairs (complements, 2^63 on one/both operands, val01/val10 offsets, swaps of tail words/blocks, +-1 additive, tail-only, cross-length zero messages, block2 := block1^(55..,AA..)) at 2^26 seeds each on the 64-bit hash with per-bit z-scores of h^h' and of h; 12 threads on the server.
res.validated_against: SMHasher3 verification values reproduced by verify.c using the procedure in lib/Hashinfo.cpp _ComputedVerifyImpl (keys {}, {0}, {0,1}, ..., seed 256-i, then hash the concatenated outputs with seed 0, first 4 LE bytes): a5hash 0xADDE79B3 OK, a5hash_128 0x89406B11 OK, a5hash_128__64 0x14AD402C OK. Upstream v5.25 a5hash.h read for structural parity only (not vector-validated).
res.summary: Two real effects. (A) a5hash128 and its 64-bit truncation are broken KEY-FREE at every length >= 17: Seed3=0xA4093822299F31D0, Seed4=0xC0AC29B7C97C50DD, Seed5..8 are unseeded constants, and the last 16 bytes (17..32 B), bytes 16..31 (33..64 B) or lanes (m1,m5),(m2,m6),(m3,m7) of the first 64-byte block (>64 B) go through PUBLIC products (u+K)(v+K') before touching seeded state; any u*v=u'*v' (e.g. u=0 kills the whole partner word: 2^64-way multicollisions) collides for every seed. 12 constructions, 2^20 seeds each, P=1, both output halves. (B) The 64-bit a5hash has a seed-skewed initial state: X gets only the odd seed bits, Y only the even ones, so v2(Seed1_init)=v2(X)+v2(Y) is controlled by the length. At len 6615 the exact probability Pr[Seed1_init = 0x8e5caae000000000] = 118*2^-45 = 2^-38.12 (exhaustive enumeration of all relevant seed bits), and every such seed makes the first 16-byte block dead, so the pair (W0=W*, W1) vs (W0=W*, W1') collides: eps >= 2^-38.1 at L=827 words, i.e. 47.8 bits (paper metric), vs 57-64 for the proven hashes. Other exact points: len 137687 eps>=2^-37.2 (51.3 bits), len 15866327 eps>=2^-32.0 exactly (52.9 bits). The initial state also has constant bits (Seed2_init bit 63 = 0 always; Seed1_init bit 0 = 0 for odd len) and 25-51 bits with |z|>=6 at 2^30 seeds. Structured pairs on the fully seeded 64-bit path (143 pairs, 2^26 seeds) give nothing: 0 collisions, max |z| 4.0.

claims.claim: a5hash_128 and a5hash_128__64 (v5.21; upstream v5.25 identical here) admit seed-independent collisions at every length >= 17: Seed3/Seed4/Seed5..8 are constants, so (c+K3)(d+K4) [17..32 B, c,d = last 16 bytes], (lu64(16)+K3)(lu64(24)+K4) [33..64 B] and the first-block lanes (m1+K3)(m5+K4), (m2+K5)(m6+K6), (m3+K7)(m7+K8) [>64 B] are public functions; any u*v = u'*v' collides, and u = 0 makes the partner 8-byte word dead (2^64-way multicollisions).
claims.evidence: Algebra from the source (Seed3 = 0xA4093822299F31D0, Seed4 = 0xC0AC29B7C97C50DD constants) plus keyfree128.c: 12 constructions at lengths 17, 24, 32, 48, 64, 100, 200, 2^20 random seeds each, 2^20/2^20 collisions on the full 128-bit output (and on the truncated variant); the same pair on the 64-bit a5hash gives 0/2^20.

(odd bits fixed); at len 6615 (p,q)=(20,17) costs 19 seed bits and the residual product X''Y'' mod 2^27 over the 2^26 relevant assignments hits 0x11cb955c 118 times (exhaustive); all 1888 conforming seeds (each assignment x 16 random upper fills) give a full a5hash64 collision (first block dead); 0 collisions in 649178 random seeds.
enum_mode.c exhaustive enumerations (logs enum_*.log), each with all conforming seeds verified to collide and a random-seed control with 0 hits.

claims.claim: The 64-bit a5hash has no public-only path: every message word is XORed into Seed1 or Seed2 (both halves of the seeded product X*Y) before any multiply; the only public relations are the read layout (len 4..7 same word in both operands, len 8 halves swapped, len 12 middle word twice) and the val01/val10 offsets.

claims.claim: Initial-state biases of the 64-bit hash: Seed2_init bit 63 = 0 for every seed and every len < 2^61 (Y < 2^63 because K1 bit 63 = 0 is a fixed odd position); Seed1_init bit 0 = 0 for every odd len (X even); Seed1_init bit 1 = X_1*Y_0 is 1 w.p. 1/4 for odd len; at len 7 bits 0 and 2 of Seed1_init are 0 always.
claims.evidence: Algebra on the product's low/high bits; init_bias.c at 2^30 seeds: p1 = 0.0000 (z = -32768) for Seed2[63], Seed1[0] (odd len), Seed1[2] (len 7); p1 = 0.2500 for Seed1[1] (odd len) and Seed2[62]; 25..51 state bits with |z| >= 6 at each of 14 lengths.

claims.evidence: pairs64.c on the server, 143 pairs x 2^26 random seeds: 0 full collisions in every pair (95% bound eps < 2^-24.4 each), max |z| of any h^h' bit 4.01 over 9152 bits, max single-message output bias |z| 3.85.

res.method: Full differential scan (label a5hash-foldscan) plus analytic structure checks. Scan: one fixed random base message per length L in {1..40, 48, 63, 64, 65, 96, 128, 160, 200}; at every 8-byte position: complement, +1, -1, +2^32, -2^32, flip bit 0/31/32/63 (=+2^63), byte+1 for each byte; paired differences on (p, p+8) inside one 16-byte block: (+1,+1), (-1,-1), (+1,-1), (-1,+1), (not,not), (+2^32,+2^32), (+2^32,-2^32), (f63,f63), (f0,f0), (f31,f31), (f32,f32); cross-length: append 0x00/0xFF/0x01, append 8 or 16 zero bytes; 11 structured key-free candidates for a5hash128. 4884 cells. Per seed both variants are evaluated on both messages; recorded: exact 64-bit collisions, trailing-zero histogram of h1^h2 (partial collisions of low 8/16/24/32/48 bits), per-bit bias of h1^h2, plus the 128-bit variant's low-word and full-128 collisions. Pass 1: 2^24 seeds per cell (seed_i = splitmix64(salt*2^48+i), salt 1). Pass 2: 2^30 seeds (salt 2, quick mode) on the 50 selected cells (top 20 by |z| of low-16 partial collisions for each variant, top 10 by low-24 partials for each variant, all kf128 cells; no cell had >= 2 hits or per-bit |z| >= 6). Extra: the same 4884 cells on an all-0x00 base (2^22, salt 3) and an all-0xFF base (2^22, salt 4). Analytic: exact prefix enumeration of the heaviest value of Seed1_init (low 28 bits exhaustive, extended by 16 then 20 seed bits; the resulting seed set is exact for the value) and direct check of the dead-first-operand pair on those seeds; exact-bit checks of the initial state on 2^16 seeds per length; sampling statistics of Seed1_init/Seed2_init at 2^28 seeds. res.caveats: (1) The a5hash version is the one registered in SMHasher3 (v5.21); upstream a5hash128 may have changed since, so the key-free result should be re-checked against the current upstream before being cited for it. (2) The weak-seed rates 2^-53.5..2^-54.6 are lower bounds from a beam-width-1 prefix search; the true heaviest Seed1_init value (and any Seed2_init-based trail) may give a somewhat larger eps; the 128-bit short-path analogue (a = -w64, len <= 16) is derived but was not checked (heavy2 stopped unfinished). (3) The generic scan resolves rates only down to ~2^-22.4 (2^24 seeds) and ~2^-28.4 (2^30 seeds); the trails above are far below its resolution and were found analytically; the scan therefore cannot rule out other structured pairs at 2^-30..2^-55. (4) One base message per length; the zero and 0xFF bases were run at 2^22 only; the paired patterns cover (p, p+8) inside one 16-byte block only; the len < 12 tail path has no dead-operand pair (A == B for len 4..7, B built from the same words as A for len 8..11) and was not attacked beyond the scan. (5) Pass 2 ran in quick mode: the per-bit bias columns (maxz64/maxz128) of results_p2.tsv are not collected and must be ignored; per-bit statistics come from pass 1 only (2^24 seeds: a bias of |z| = 6 corresponds to a relative bias of 2^-10.4). (6) Cells 3304/3308/3314 (and similar +2^32 / f32 / b4+1 triples where the base bit is 0 and no carry occurs) generate identical second messages, so the 4873 generic cells contain some duplicates. (7) initstate's low-28 histogram saturates at 255 (len 2, 3, 7 report 255 = lower bound); heavy.c uses exact counts. (8) Score implications: a5hash128 ~ log2(L) bits (probability-1 key-free collisions); a5hash64 <= ~54.6 bits (eps >= 2^-53.52 at 17 bytes = 2.1 words), i.e. below the proven hashes (57-64) but above wyhash/rapidhash/XXH3 (~27-29).

res.method: Evolutionary search over attacker-fixed message pairs (m, m2) against a uniformly random hidden 64-bit seed. Own single-file C transcription of a5hash (64 and 128-bit). Islands of POP=24 (ELITE=6); every generation all candidates are evaluated on a fresh common batch of 2^15 seeds (2^16 locally) and survivors accumulate statistics across generations. Objectives: full-output collisions, low-12/16/24/32-bit partial collisions per output half, max per-bit |z| of the XOR and the additive output differences per half (bit-sliced counters), combined into a bits-of-surprise score (-log2 Poisson/normal tail p-value, Bonferroni-corrected per family). Mutations: single-bit flips (m2 only / both), byte +-1 (m2 / both), 32-bit word +-2^k (m2 / both), 64-bit word +-2^k, XOR-difference move between words, base randomisation keeping the difference (whole / one word), structured 32/64-bit differences (all-ones, top bit, +-1, +-2^k, +2^32), second structured difference, length change within class, cross-length (l2 = l1 +- 1), dropping a byte difference, crossovers (per-word difference from another elite; other elite's base with own difference); 1/16 fresh random structured pairs. One run per length class (short 1..16, mid 17..32, block 33..64, long 65..160) per variant (64, 128): 8 server runs x 2 threads x 840 s = 361,125 generations, plus 2 local runs (64-bit short/mid, 500 s) = 12,236 generations; ~2^38.1 seed evaluations, ~2^22.7 distinct candidate pairs. Then the top-5 distinct pairs per run (50 pairs, 70 output halves) were re-measured at 2^28 fresh seeds each (16 threads, seed stream disjoint from the search's) with z-scores.
res.validated_against: SMHasher3 verification procedure (lib/Hashinfo.cpp _ComputedVerifyImpl: keys {},{0},{0,1},... of length i hashed with seed 256-i, outputs concatenated and hashed with seed 0, low 32 bits LE) reproduced exactly for all three registered variants: a5hash 64-bit 0xADDE79B3, a5hash_128 0x89406B11, a5hash_128__64 (truncated) 0x14AD402C. Null-control measurements on hand-written random pairs at 2^26/2^27 seeds gave nominal statistics (max |z| 2.3-3.4, c24 within Poisson noise).
res.summary: No effect found for a5hash (64-bit or 128-bit) by evolutionary search over message pairs. Across ~2^38 seed evaluations of ~2^22.7 candidate pairs in all four length classes, no candidate ever produced a full-output collision; the best search-time scores (8-13 bits, on 2^18-2^19 seeds) were selection noise: at 2^28 fresh seeds all 50 top pairs are null (0 full collisions, low-24-bit collisions per half mean 15.9 vs 16.0 expected, range 7-25; low-32-bit collisions 5 total vs 4.4 expected; max per-bit |z| 3.94 over 8960 tests, the nominal extreme). The per-pair collision probability of every pair reached is bounded above by ~2^-26.4 (95%, zero hits in 2^28) and is consistent with the 2^-64 floor; no per-bit bias with |z| >= 6 exists for any of them.

claims.claim: The single-file a5hash transcription (64-bit and 128-bit, incl. the truncated 128->64 variant) is exact.
claims.evidence: verify.c reproduces the SMHasher3 _ComputedVerifyImpl values 0xADDE79B3 (a5hash), 0x89406B11 (a5hash_128) and 0x14AD402C (a5hash_128__64), identical to the registered verification_LE constants in smhasher3 hashes/a5hash.cpp.

claims.claim: No candidate pair in the evolutionary search ever produced a full-output collision (64- or 128-bit) for any evaluated seed.
claims.evidence: 0 lines with full>=1 across all hall-of-fame outputs and progress logs of the 8 server runs (361,125 generations x 24 candidates x 2^15 seeds) and 2 local runs (12,236 generations x 24 x 2^16), i.e. ~2^38.1 seed evaluations over ~2^22.7 distinct candidate pairs spanning lengths 1..160 in both variants.

claims.claim: The top-5 distinct pairs of every run (50 pairs, 70 output halves) show no collision excess and no per-bit bias at 2^28 fresh seeds each.
claims.evidence: server/remeasure.jsonl: full collisions 0/50; low-24-bit collisions per half mean 15.87 (expected 16.0; min 7, max 25, consistent with Poisson(16) over 70 draws); low-32-bit collisions 5 total (expected 4.4); max |z| over 8960 per-bit tests of the XOR and additive output differences = 3.94, the nominal extreme for that many normal draws; no |z| >= 6 anywhere.

claims.claim: The search-time scores of the best candidates (8-13 bits of surprise on 2^18-2^19 seeds) were entirely selection noise, not a property of the pairs.
claims.evidence: Every one of the 50 re-measured pairs regressed to null at 2^28 (e.g. the 64-bit len-4 pair with 2 low-24 hits in 2^18 seeds shows 20 low-24 hits in 2^28, expectation 16); the null controls on hand-written random pairs at 2^26/2^27 give the same statistics (max |z| 2.3-3.4).

claims.claim: For every pair the search reached, the seed-averaged collision probability eps is below 2^-26.4 (95%) and is consistent with the generic 2^-64 floor; a5hash has no message-pair collision structure reachable by local hill-climbing on partial-collision and bias objectives.
claims.evidence: Zero full collisions in 2^28 seeds per pair gives the 95% upper bound only; the extrapolation to the 2^-64 floor and to pairs outside the ~2^22.7 candidates visited is unproven. An algebraic (key-free or weak-seed) structure that gives no partial-collision or per-bit gradient would be invisible to this search.

res.caveats: (1) Negative result of a heuristic search: the mutation operators are local (bit/byte/word moves, structured 32/64-bit differences, difference moves, crossovers) and the objectives are partial collisions and per-bit biases; an algebraic collision structure with no gradient in those objectives would not be found, and the ~2^22.7 candidate pairs are a vanishing fraction of the pair space. (2) Search-time statistics were on 2^15-2^16 seeds per generation (cumulative 2^18-2^19 for the reported survivors), so the search could only ever detect effects with eps >~ 2^-20 or per-bit biases >~ 1%; only the 2^28 re-measurement (eps upper bound ~2^-26.4 per pair, bias resolution ~4 sigma at |bias| ~ 2^-13) is the honest measurement. (3) rate_log2 = -26.4 in the pairs table is the 95% one-sided upper bound from zero hits in 2^28 seeds, not an observed rate. (4) The a5hash_32 variant (32-bit seed) was not searched. (5) Because the run budget was ~14 min per class instead of 25, and the first server launch had to be restarted after a bug (identical-message pairs for lengths < 4 were admitted as candidates; fixed before the reported runs), coverage is what is stated above and nothing more. (6) The local M2 runs used 2^16 seeds/generation and 1 thread each; their outputs were re-measured on the server with the same 2^28 protocol.

res.method: Multi-seed SMT (z3 4.15.4 local / 5.1.0 on the server via pip --user): exact 64-bit bit-vector model of the short path and one 16-byte block (len <= 32), 128-bit products via ZeroExt+Extract; K hard-coded random seeds, symbolic message pair, optional byte/word difference restrictions, seed classes with 32 fixed bits, CEGIS option. 20 queries at a 420 s box each (16 parallel on <xeon-host>). Because the solver decided nothing, the effect reported comes from the companion analysis: exact class-conditional statements read off the source and checked on 2^16 seeds (checks.c), per-bit bias of the init words at 2^28 seeds (bias.c), multi-resolution mode density of S2i at 2^32 seeds (dens.c), and exact multiplicities of specific S2i values over all 2^64 seeds by enumerating the 2^32 u-operands and solving for v (findseed.c). Explicit pairs measured over 2^24 random seeds (measure.c).
res.validated_against: SMHasher3 HashInfo::_ComputedVerifyImpl reproduced from source/smhasher3-mr-seeddiff/lib/Hashinfo.cpp: my C reference gives 0xADDE79B3 (a5hash 64), 0x89406B11 (a5hash_128) and 0x14AD402C (a5hash_128__64), all matching the registered values. The z3 model agrees with the C reference on 140/140 random (seed, message) cases covering every length 0..32 (>= 20 per path), locally and on the server.
res.summary: The multi-seed SMT method fails outright on a5hash: 19 of 20 queries (len 3..32, K = 1..3, free / one-byte / one-word / block-word differences, two 32-fixed-bit seed classes) returned unknown at 420 s, including K = 1 cases where a solution provably exists (w1 = S1i(seed) gives output 0); only len 1, K = 2 was decided (UNSAT, 97 s). The real finding is structural: a5hash's final fold returns exactly 0 whenever hi64(x*y) = 0 for the pre-final state (x, y), and its init word S2i = hi64(u*v) (u, v carrying the odd/even seed bits) is far from uniform: top bit always 0, range [2^59.1, 2^62.8], mode density 12.6/22.3/39.7/76.6/125 x uniform at 8/12/16/20/24-bit resolution, and exact multiplicities 131-159 (vs 2 on average) for several values with prefix 0a1fce. Consequently a fixed 16-byte pair with w2 = 0x0a1fce0000000001 and any w1 != w1' collides with probability at least 159/2^64 = 2^-56.7 (exact count), and a 24-byte pair with the block word W2 = that value collides whenever S2i = W2 (dead operand); the union with the 'both products < 2^64' event is conjectured near 2^-52. In the paper's score this puts a5hash at about 57.7 bits proven-by-enumeration (L = 2 words), about 53 conjectured, below the 2^-64 floor but nowhere near the wyhash/MUM class. Output bits show no bias (|z| <= 2.7 at 2^28).

Exact multiplicity of this S2i value over all 2^64 seeds = 159 (findseed, enumeration of all 2^32 u operands). Superset event: hi64((S1i^w1)(S2i^w2)) = 0 for both messages (proved from the source, 65536/65536 in checks.c A); second witness seed 0297065ea9fc0e9d has S2i = 0a1fce0000000000 so y = 1.

res.caveats: The assigned method (multi-seed SMT) produced no SAT model at all: every query is unknown at the 420 s box except one UNSAT, so the seed-class and CEGIS branches were never exercised beyond their first round; the effect reported was found by direct analysis, not by the solver. The 2^24-seed measurements of the explicit pairs show 0 hits, as expected at 2^-56.7; the collision statements are exact (proved from the source, checked on 2^16 seeds with seed-constructed messages, and verified at explicit witness seeds), and the 159/2^64 rate is an exact enumeration count for len 16 only. The len-24 multiplicity of h* and the dens.c duplicate phase (2^31-sample qsort) did not finish within the time budget. The ~2^-52 union estimate is a conjecture resting on unmeasured density between 24 and 64 bits of resolution and on fine-scale independence of S1i's and S2i's top bits. The a5hash128 128-bit output does not collide under these classes (731/65536 in class E is an artefact of tiny products); only its low word / the truncated variant do. Only the SMHasher3-registered v5.21 was analysed; upstream may differ.

res.hash: MuseAir v0.3 (SMHasher3 hashes/museair.cpp: MuseAir, MuseAir__bfast, MuseAir_128, MuseAir_128__bfast)
res.method: Structure and key-free constructions. Wrote down, from the SMHasher3 source, every point where a message word meets the seed-dependent state and every point where it passes through a public function only; enumerated the code paths (len<=16, 17..32, 33..47, 48..95, >=96) and the overlapping reads (read_short off=0/4, the last-16-byte re-read). Built a single-file implementation (museair.h, all four variants) validated against the SMHasher3 verification procedure, then constructed explicit pairs for each structural weakness and tested them on random seeds and on the exact seed classes (local Apple M2 Pro <=3 threads, server x86 16 threads). Constructions: (A) len 17..32: the tail (u,v) enters ONLY via the public G(u,v)=(lo(C2(C3^u))^hi(C4(C5^v)), lo(C4(C5^v))^hi(C2(C3^u))) xored into (i,j), and read_short on the first 16 bytes is a public bijection onto (i,j), so any two distinct tails with a compensated prefix give identical state for every seed. (B) len 41..47 bfast: the final mumix is on (s2,s5) with s2^s5=C2^C5 public and the bfast mumix (p,q)<-(lo,hi)((p^ip)(q^iq)) is symmetric, so swapping operands (m_a'=m_b^K, m_b'=m_a^K, shared window bytes pinned) collides key-free. res.method: Weak-seed classes and seed-expansion structure. Own single-file implementation (museair.h) of all four variants. Every multiply was written with both operands as functions of (seed, message). Short path: seed enters only through (lo2,hi2)=(seed^C0)*(len^C1) into i=m_i^len^lo2, j=m_j^seed^hi2, then a seed-free 2-round multiply finaliser; the seed->(i,j) map is injective, so any class that makes the state public or an operand zero is a 1-seed event; measured per-bit biases, top/low-16-bit min-entropy and mode of lo2, hi2, seed^hi2 and the bfast round-A swap value lo2^hi2^seed over 2^26 random seeds (dist.c; 2^30 runs still in flight on the server). Long path (len>=33): initial state s0=C0+seed, s1=C1-seed, s2=C2^seed, s3=C3+seed, s4=C4-seed, s5=C5^seed; every product in the first block/lane pass has operands (s_a ^ words, s_b ^ words) with s_a ^ s_b a skewed function of the seed (s2^s5 = C2^C5 exactly). In the bfast variants a mumix/ring step REPLACES the state by the 128-bit product, which is symmetric, so swapping the two operands by a matched XOR difference (plus one compensating XOR on the next shared word in the ring) gives an identical state whenever s_a ^ s_b equals the chosen value T. The probability of s_a ^ s_b = T is the probability of one carry pattern of b^(b+S'), computed exactly by a DP over carries (swapdp.py): the class is the coset where the pinned carry-choice bits of the seed match, density exactly 2^-cost, and the collision is deterministic inside it. Pairs were tested over 2^28 uniformly random seeds and over 2^28 seeds sampled directly from each class, on all four variants (non-bfast as controls), plus a short-path battery of structured XOR differences at 2^28 seeds and an explicit two-seed floor construction for the bfast short path.

res.summary: Both bfast variants (MuseAir__bfast 64 and MuseAir_128__bfast) are broken by seed-expansion structure: (1) KEY-FREE collision for every seed at lengths 41..47 bytes: the lane (s2,s5)=(C2^seed,C5^seed) is untouched until the final mumix on the last 16 bytes, and since the bfast mumix replaces the state by the product of (s2^t0)*(s5^t1), the pair t0'=t1^(C2^C5), t1'=t0^(C2^C5) (with the bytes overlapping words 2-3 held fixed by choice of t1) gives the same product and the same output: 2^20/2^20 seeds collide at every length 41..47 (0/2^20 for the non-bfast variants). eps=1 at L=41 B (5.1 words) -> bits ~ 2.4. (2) At every length >= 33 the bfast variants have weak-seed classes of density exactly 2^-21 (pairs (s2,s3) and (s4,s5)), 2^-22 ((s0,s1),(s1,s2),(s0,s3),(s1,s4)) and 2^-23 ((s3,s4)) with conditional collision probability 1: operand swap of a bfast product, i.e. XOR the class value T into the two operand words (and into the next shared word for the 96-byte ring). Random-seed rates measured at 2^28 seeds match the DP densities (e.g. 118-138 hits for cost 21, 46-75 for cost 22, 34 for cost 23) and class-sampled seeds collide 2^28/2^28 in every case. Best total rate for bfast at len>=48: 2^-21 (bits ~ 21+log2(6) ~ 23.6 at 48 B); at 41..47 B: rate 1. The non-bfast variants (MuseAir 64 and MuseAir_128, whose short path has no bfast at all) showed 0 hits at 2^28 random and 2^28 class-sampled seeds on every one of the same pairs and on the short-path battery: the XOR-feedback (state ^= lo/hi, state += lo^hi) keeps the pre-product operands in the state, so every neutralising class found needs a full 64-bit event (an operand equal to 0, 1, or a fixed constant), i.e. the floor 2^-64; the best construction found is 2 seeds (2^-63) and only for bfast-64 short messages. Short-path derived words: hi2 < len^C1 always (top bit 1 with p=0.151, z=-5712 at 2^26), seed^hi2 top bit p=0.349 (z=-2480) with 11.0/16 bits min-entropy in its top 16 bits; for odd len lo2 has tz(len^C1) forced-zero low bits (5 bits at len 9); none of these biases yields a collision class above the floor because seed->(i,j) is injective.

res.caveats: Lengths are in bytes (paper's L in 8-byte words = len/8). The seed-class densities are exact by the carry argument, and the conditional rate 1 follows from the operand symmetry, but the exhaustive in-class check is 2^28 seeds per pair, not the full 2^43 coset. The 2^30 distribution runs requested for the short-path words did not finish on the loaded server within the budget; the reported biases are at 2^26 seeds (z-scores scale by 4 at 2^30) and agree with the analytic values (hi2 < len^C1). The non-bfast verdict is a conjecture from this method's class enumeration and the tested differences; the key-free 17..32-byte lead (public products C2*(C3^u), C4*(C5^v)) is a different method and was not attempted here. In the ring, product 5's class needs len >= 104 (at 96 B the tail re-reads word 10) and product 6 has no class (its first operand is already a product). The bfast short path (len <= 32) has only the 2-seed floor construction; the 128-bit variants share one short path in which the bfast flag has no effect, so their short-path behaviour equals MuseAir_128.

res.hash: MuseAir v0.3 (SMHasher3 hashes/museair.cpp): MuseAir, MuseAir__bfast, MuseAir_128, MuseAir_128__bfast
res.method: Full differential scan (harness family, extended) + an algebraic key-free construction. Single-file reimplementation ma.c computes all four variants in one pass per (message, seed). Cell family per length L in 1..40, 48, 63, 64, 65, 96, 128, 160, 200 on a fixed random base message: 'single' differences on 8-byte windows at offsets 0,4,8,... (step 8 for L>=96) plus tail-aligned L-8, L-12, L-16, on 4-byte windows at the short-path read offsets (0, 4, L-4, L-8, 16, 20, L-12), and on the short path's virtual 64-bit operands i=(m[0..4)<<32|m[L-4..L)), j=(m[4..8)<<32|m[L-8..L-4)), u, v; types: complement, +1, -1, +2^32, -2^32, flip bit 0/31/32/63 (=+2^63); 'byte': +1 and complement on every byte (L>=96: first/last 24 bytes and every 8th byte); 'pair-same': same difference on two windows that meet in one product (i/j and u/v operands and their 4-byte halves; adjacent aligned 8-byte words and the tail pair (L-16,L-8) on the long path; includes all-ones on both operands); 'pair-opp': +d/-d on the two windows; 'xlen': append 00, prepend 00, zero-pad to 8, truncate 1. Total 6157 cells. Pass 1: 2^24 uniformly random 64-bit seeds per cell (splitmix64 stream 1), counting full collisions of the 64-bit, 64-bit bfast, 128-bit, 128-bit bfast outputs and of the low word of the 128-bit outputs, lo32/lo16 partial collisions with z-scores, and per-bit bias of h(m)^h(m') on every 8th seed (2^21 per cell). Pass 2: 2^30 seeds (independent stream 2) on the 20 best cells by |z16| plus the 10 most bit-biased (no cell had >=2 hits). Server <xeon-host>, 16 threads, ~11 min + ~5 min wall. Key-free lead (17..32 B): with a=C3^u, b=C5^v, a'=a+da, b'=b+db, the u/v contributions to (i,j) coincide for every seed when C4*db == swap64(C2*da) as 128-bit integers and the four 64-bit additions are carry-free; the (da,db) equation is a 2-D affine lattice problem (kf_lattice.py, Gauss reduction; C2 is even and gcd(2^128-1, C4)=3 so a general congruence solver is used) with exactly one solution in the box, and a, b were found by random search over carry-free lo words (kf.c, ~2^31 tries).
res.validated_against: ./ma verify reproduces all four SMHasher3 verification values (MuseAir 0xF89F1683, MuseAir__bfast 0xC61BEE56, MuseAir_128 0xD3DFE238, MuseAir_128__bfast 0x27939BF1) with the procedure of lib/Hashinfo.cpp (keys {0..i-1}, seed 256-i, i=0..255, then hash the concatenation with seed 0, low 4 bytes LE; Seed() is the identity for MuseAir). The key-free pair was additionally hashed by SMHasher3's own hashes/museair.cpp (compiled from a registration-stripped copy, smh/drv.cpp): 2^18 seeds, all four variants collide, seed-0 output 0xe7fc798231f1e896 identical to my implementation.
res.summary: FOUND: a seed-independent (P = 1) collision for MuseAir v0.3 at 32 bytes that holds for all four variants (64-bit, bfast, 128-bit, 128-bit bfast), for every seed, and for every choice of the first 16 bytes. m = 101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1f3edfaa2763ccd3e8f8e5d00dc73236e4, m' = 101112131415161718191a1b1c1d1e1f99b0519651a489b815f5132911d93af1. The u/v words of the 17..32-byte short path enter the state only through i ^= lo(C2*(C3^u)) ^ hi(C4*(C5^v)), j ^= lo(C4*(C5^v)) ^ hi(C2*(C3^u)) -- public functions of the message -- and da = 0xb0e896630cf3a6b6, db = 0x302997ce1c430f6d satisfy C4*db == swap64(C2*da) exactly (the unique point of the corresponding 2-D lattice in the box), so with a = 0x0689ecaac63db690, b = 0x3a9ce9f3cd6c0bd0 (all four 64-bit additions carry-free) both (i, j) contributions are identical: lo0^hi1 = 0x6a03821811c10404 and lo1^hi0 = 0x2a30d32201014728 for both messages. Verified: 2^20 random seeds (my code), 2^20 random (prefix, seed) pairs, 2^18 seeds with SMHasher3's own museair.cpp -- 100 % collisions everywhere. In the paper's metric this puts MuseAir at bits = log2(4 words / 1) = 2, i.e. in the MUM class (key-free break), for all four variants. The family for this (da, db) has ~1.2e4 valid a times ~3.6e3 valid b (~4e7 quadruples), each with 2^128 free prefixes. The generic differential scan itself is entirely null: 6157 cells x 2^24 seeds gave 0 full-output collisions in every cell and every output column (eps < 2^-22.4 per cell at 95 %), lo32 partials 51 vs 48 expected, z16 mean -0.001 / sd 1.001 / max 4.31 over 12,314 cell-variants, per-bit max |z| 4.96 over ~788k bit tests (54 with |z|>=4 vs ~50 expected); pass 2 at 2^30 on 30 cells: 0 full collisions (eps < 2^-28.4 per cell), |z16| <= 2.22, per-bit max |z| 3.72 at 2^27 samples, 22 lo32 partials vs 15 expected -- no pass-1 outlier replicated. So none of the complement / +-1 / +-2^32 / +2^63 / single-bit / byte / paired / cross-length differences on a random base has a detectable seed-averaged effect; MuseAir's only weakness found is the structural, seed-free one.
