res.method: Evolutionary search over message pairs (label museair-hillclimb): population 24 + 72 children per generation, every candidate re-evaluated each generation on a FRESH batch of 2^15 seeds on all four variants, score = clipped z of max per-bit bias (XOR and additive output difference, both words for 128-bit) + clipped z of low-16/low-24 partial collisions + large bonuses for low-32 / 64-bit-half / full collisions, EMA over re-evaluations. Mutations: single-bit flip, byte +/-1, 32-bit half-word +/-2^k at any byte offset, 64-bit word +/-2^k, move XOR difference between 8-byte windows, rebase keeping XOR or additive difference, crossover (difference from another candidate; byte splice), length +/-1, cross-length, fresh low-weight pair. One run per length class on <xeon-host> (4 threads x 1500 s each): short 1..32 B (5196 generations), mid 33..95 (5051), block 96..191 (4626), long 192..400 (4034); ~4.6e5-5.0e5 candidate pairs per class. Top 5 distinct pairs per class re-measured at 2^28 seeds per variant (16 threads). Separately, the structured 17..32-byte lead was tested with a carry-vector DP construction (keyfree32.py).
res.validated_against: Own single-file implementation museair.h reproduces the SMHasher3 verification procedure (lib/Hashinfo.cpp _ComputedVerifyImpl: keys {},{0},{0,1},...,255 bytes with seed 256-i, then hash the 256 concatenated outputs with seed 0, low 32 bits) for all four variants: F89F1683 (MuseAir), C61BEE56 (bfast), D3DFE238 (128), 27939BF1 (128 bfast). hinfo->Seed() is the identity for MuseAir (no seedfn registered).
res.summary: The generic evolutionary search found nothing above noise in any length class: 0 full collisions in 20 pairs x 4 variants x 2^28 seeds, max per-bit bias |z| = 3.99 over ~15,000 z-values (expected max ~4.0), partial-collision z within [-1.8, 2.75]; one 259-byte long-class pair had 5 low-32-bit partial hits across six output words (0.375 expected) at 2^28, but the 2^30 superset run added 0 new hits where 1.1 were expected (Poisson tail 0.019): noise. The search has no gradient because the seed-dependent finalisation scrambles any pre-finalisation state difference. The structured lead is real and stronger than stated: for 17 <= len <= 32 the second read_short words enter only through the seed-free products C2*(C3^u) and C4*(C5^v) as i ^= lo0^hi1, j ^= lo1^hi0, so a 32-byte pair with equal first 16 bytes and equal (lo0^hi1, lo1^hi0) collides for EVERY seed in ALL FOUR variants: eps = 1 (key-free). Constructed by a 64-step DP over carry vectors (the lead's details were wrong: C2 is divisible by 4, and hi(C4*y) < 2^59 so a 2^63 difference there is impossible); solutions for every k = 2..9 tried, 40 ms each. Verified: 3 pairs x 2^20 seeds locally, 1 pair x 2^28 seeds on the server, plus seeds 0, 1, 0xdeadbeefcafef00d, 2^64-1 explicitly: 100% collisions in all four variants.

res.method: Exact z3 bit-vector models of the short/mid paths (MuseAir 0..32 B x4 variants, a5hash 0..32 B, komihash 0..31 B), validated against a single-file C implementation on 20 random (seed,msg) per length (3940 checks, 0 mismatches). Query (1) multi-seed SMT (K=2, free/u2w differences) on the server: 16 instances, all 'unknown' at 600 s (variable-by-variable 64x64->128 products defeat the bit-blaster; even komihash len 1, K=1 is unknown at 60 s). Query (3) MuseAir 17..32 B key-free system: direct z3 unknown at 600 s, so reduced algebraically: u,v enter only through public products C2*(C3^u), C4*(C5^v), so with x=C3^u, y=C5^v a pair with equal first 16 bytes collides for every seed iff (C2 x) XOR (C2 x') == swap64((C4 y) XOR (C4 y')) on 128-bit products. Step 1: exact additive difference C2*d == swap64(C4*delta) found by Lagrange reduction of the rank-2 kernel lattice of [[C2,0,-1,-2^64],[0,C4,-2^64,-1]]. Step 2: characterised achievable XOR-difference patterns of A + Delta via carries (P achievable iff P_0=Delta_0 and P_i=0 => P_{i+1}=Delta_i^Delta_{i+1}); DP picked a 42-fixed-bit pattern common to both sides. Step 3: found x, y with the prescribed product bits by MSB-first / LSB-first DFS with interval pruning (server, seconds). Step 4: measured pairs over 2^24 random seeds in C.
res.validated_against: C implementation reproduces SMHasher3 verification values (lib/Hashinfo.cpp procedure): MuseAir 0xF89F1683, MuseAir_bfast 0xC61BEE56, MuseAir_128 0xD3DFE238, MuseAir_128_bfast 0x27939BF1, a5hash 0xADDE79B3, and all 63 published komihash README vectors (seeds 0, 0x0123456789abcdef, 256); verified on both the M2 and the x86 server. z3 models validated against that C library on 3940 concrete cases.
res.summary: MuseAir v0.3 is broken key-free: explicit 32-byte message pairs collide for EVERY 64-bit seed in all four variants (64-bit, bfast, 128-bit, 128-bit bfast); measured 16777216/16777216 collisions over 2^24 random seeds on 4 pairs x 4 variants, and the underlying identity holds exactly in integer arithmetic. Hence eps = 1 at L = 4 words and MuseAir scores bits = log2(4/1) = 2. Cause: in the short path (17..32 B) the bytes 16..len enter only through seed-independent products C2*(C3^u) and C4*(C5^v) XORed cross-wise into (i, j); the pair is constructed from the exact lattice identity C2*d = swap64(C4*delta) (d = b0e896630cf3a6b6, delta = 302997ce1c430f6d) plus carry-pattern alignment. Generic multi-seed SMT (query 1) returned unknown on all 16 instances for all three hashes; a5hash and komihash: no effect found (no coverage claimed beyond the timed-out SMT runs).

res.caveats: (1) The break is at length 32 only in this run; lengths 24..31 have overlapping u/v reads (fewer free bits) and were not constructed, and lengths 17..23 have u == v or v == 0 (very few options), so the eps = 1 result is claimed for L = 4 words. (2) The multi-seed SMT queries (1) gave no information (all unknown at 600 s); query (2) (seed classes, symbolic seed) and restricted-difference variants were not run for lack of time, so a5hash and komihash carry no new negative coverage from this run. (3) The measurement uses a splitmix64 seed stream, not true randomness; the collision is however proved algebraically to hold for every seed, and the identity was also checked exactly in integers. (4) SMHasher3's museair.cpp is v0.3; upstream may have changed the short path since -- the claim is against the vendored v0.3 source only. (5) Local z3 runs on the whole key-free system never finished; the result came from the lattice + carry-pattern reduction and the DFS, not from z3 directly.
